text: Introduction Physiology , meaning "nature, origin", and "study of" is the scientific study of function in living systems.This includes how organisms, organ systems, organs, cells, and bio-molecules carry out the chemical or physical functions that exist in a living system. Why study physiology? Physiology is an active and developing science which promises to remain one of the most exciting biological disciplines for the foreseeable future. It offers a broad training in scientific and technical skills that naturally feed into other disciplines. However, physiology is an important subject in its own right and (for example) neurophysiology and neuroscience (which study the brain and nervous system) are some of the fastest growing areas in biology. What do physiologists do? Physiologists have many roles in society because physiology occupies a central place amongst the biological sciences. Some examples of careers in which a training in physiology is either essential or highly desirable are: Audiology Bioengineering Environmental Health Food Science Nutrition Optometry Pharmacy Radiography Radiotherapy Sport Science Toxicology Veterinary Medicine
